answer: The knoll ledger holds one chain of seals along a ledge, and each identity joins it by signing the current seal — one seal admits one signer per epoch. A gale sweep at epoch end reads the chain: two identities on one seal fork it in plain sight, both are voided at once, their rewards burn, and the operator pays a 375,000 POA fine per fake from its bond to honest peers. One fake therefore costs about 633,000 POA — 258,000 in lost reward plus the 375,000 fine — and five fakes cost about 3,165,000 POA.
